pages.text: A full spool holds $(item)1000 turns$() of wire. There are three: $(item)Copper$(), $(item)Aluminum$() and $(item)Constantan$(). $(l)Making spools - $(item)Empty Spool$():$() cut $(item)Hardened Planks$() in a Stonecutter. $(li)Crafting: surround an Empty Spool with $(item)8 wires$() of one metal.

The spool comes out full, 1000 turns. $(li)Winding: put $(item)wire$() in the Winding Machine's workpiece slot with an empty spool, or a spool of the same metal, mounted. Each wire gives $(item)125 turns$(), wound one per tick, up to 1000. Wire goes in one at a time, so feed it with a funnel.

A spool whose turns run out turns back into an $(item)Empty Spool$(), ready to be refilled.$(br2)$(l)Laying cables$()$(br)Spools are also how you lay cables between connectors: click one connector, then the other. A run costs $(item)125 turns per 8 blocks$() of length. If the spool does not have enough turns left for that run, it tells you and nothing is placed.
Copper wire makes the coils, constantan wire makes resistors.
